newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq silent on Clinton's election triumph.
newsitem.headline: Iraq silent on Clinton's election triumph.

text.p: The Iraqi government and state-controlled media made no immediate comment on Wednesday on the election triumph of U.S. President Bill Clinton, who has ordered two rounds of missile attacks on Iraq.
Iraqi state-run radio did not even mention Clinton's re-election in their news bulletins. Government newspapers went to press before the announcement of the results.

Iraq's media has already said it made no difference who won the election because Washington's policy would not change towards Iraq, under U.N. sanctions since it invaded Kuwait in 1990. A U.S.-led force drove its troops out in 1991.

"The world will see today (Tuesday) the election of a new U.S. president and at the same time it will witness a U.S. policy based on hegemony and anarchy using its military might to serve its own policy to which only Iraq has said 'No'," the official al-Iraq paper had said.
Iraq's reaction to the outcome of this year's U.S. election is slower in coming than in 1992 when Iraq's 1991 Gulf War foe George Bush was defeated by Clinton.
Bush's defeat was welcomed by Baghdad and there were country-wide celebrations.

During his first term, Clinton ordered two major missile strikes against Iraq, one in June 1993 and the second in September 1996. The first was in retaliation for an alleged plot by Iraq to assassinate Bush. The second was sparked by Baghdad sending troops to its north to decide an inter-Kurdish conflict.
Many Iraqis, suffering under tough U.N. trade sanctions see a better chance of the curbs being lifted under Clinton than Bob Dole, the candidate of former president Bush's Republican party.
